about: The areas of a Deathbot conversation. It is a map, not a checklist: people cover them in any order and need not cover them all. At a natural pause, let the person decide whether to stay with what they are on, talk about something else, or stop; suggest an unexplored area when it would help with what they are trying to understand. Guidance for each is in guide/conversation.md. A harness can show this map to the person; 'start' is what the person would say to go there.

areas.title: Who speaks for you
areas.start: Let's talk about who would speak for me if I couldn't.
areas.covers: Who the doctors would turn to; whether that is who they would choose; whether that person is willing, what they understand, and how much judgement they should have; a backup.

areas.title: You and your health
areas.start: Let me tell you about me and my health.
areas.covers: Their life and people; their conditions and outlook as they understand them.

areas.title: What matters most
areas.start: Let's talk about what matters most to me.
areas.covers: What makes a good day; what they would not want to live without; fears; deaths they have seen.

areas.title: What the treatments are really like
areas.start: Tell me what the treatments are really like for someone like me.
areas.covers: The treatments and situations most likely for this person, each with its alternatives and honest odds. Add a separate item for a specific treatment when it gets its own discussion.

areas.title: The hard trade-offs
areas.start: Let's talk through the hard trade-offs.
areas.covers: Where the things they care about pull against each other, and how they weigh them; time-limited trials.

areas.title: Would they know what to do?
areas.start: Let's test whether the person speaking for me would know what to do.
areas.covers: Two or three concrete scenarios: what would the proxy decide, and would they know?

areas.title: Get it written down
areas.start: Let's get what we have written down.
areas.covers: The 'What matters to me' summary in their words, reviewed and corrected by them.

areas.title: Tell the people who need to know
areas.start: Help me tell the people who need to know.
areas.covers: Who should have 'What matters to me', how it reaches them, and talking it through with the person who speaks for them.

areas.title: Bring in your health records
areas.start: I'd like to bring in my health records.
areas.covers: Working from their actual records. Only where the environment can receive them.

areas.title: Make it official
areas.start: Let's talk about making this official.
areas.covers: The state's health care proxy form and living will; for someone seriously ill or frail, portable medical orders (POLST) with their clinician.

areas.title: See what it looks like
areas.start: Show me what these situations look like.
areas.covers: Pictures of care scenes. Only where the environment can make them; see guide/images.md.
